Bidder Inquiries.Short description: Roadway Excavation and Imported Borrow Quantity inconsistencies
Bidder Inquiries.Response:
2026-10-09 07:31:18 - Poh Chu Bennetzen (Response)
[code]Your inquiry is being reviewed.[/code]
Bidder Inquiries.Question:
After reviewing the Earthwork Summary on Sheet Q-1 we have identified several inconsistencies that affect the calculation and verification of the Roadway Excavation and Imported Borrow quantities.

Here are some noted examples of the inconsistencies:

 

  1. Negative Embankment Quantities

Several locations show negative embankment quantities. Please clarify the basis for the negative embankment quantities and how these values were developed. If the negative quantities represent removal of previously placed embankment, surcharge removal, over excavation, or another condition, please identify where this work is shown in the plans and how it is intended to be accounted for in the earthwork balance.

 

  1. Locations Showing Roadway Excavation and Imported Borrow but No Embankment

Several locations on the Q sheets show roadway excavation and import borrow, but no embankment quantities. Most alarming, roundabout #1 and roundabout #2 (RA1 and RA2), as we know these are significant fill areas based on the cross-sections and need for PVD’s. However, the Earthwork Summary shows substantial quantities of both Roadway Excavation and Imported Borrow while listing no corresponding embankment quantity.

Examples include:

    • RA1: 47,833 CY Roadway Excavation and 46,648 CY Imported Borrow, no embankment quantity
    • RA2: 116,522 CY Roadway Excavation and 116,434 CY Imported Borrow, no embankment quantity

Given that these areas appear to require significant fill to reach proposed grades, please clarify:

    • Why no embankment quantities are shown for these locations.
    • Whether the excavation quantities represent over excavation, unsuitable material removal, surcharge removal, or another condition.
    • Whether these quantities are associated with ground improvement, settlement mitigation, preload embankments, or other geotechnical requirements.

 

  1. Fill Areas with Embankment Quantities but No Corresponding Import Borrow

The Earthwork Summary also appears to contain locations where significant embankment quantities are reported, but the reported Roadway Excavation quantities appear insufficient to construct the required fill and no Imported Borrow quantity is assigned to the location.

Examples include:

    • TRN2: 120 CY Roadway Excavation and 49,066 CY of embankment, no imported borrow
    • R2: 624 CY Roadway Excavation and 69,440 CY of embankment, no imported Borrow

 

    1. Overall Project Earthwork Balance

The project totals shown on Sheet Q-1 indicate:

    • Roadway Excavation: 334,533 CY
    • Embankment: 228,824 CY
    • Imported Borrow: 236,262 CY

Based on these totals, the calculated imported borrow requirement does not appear to reconcile with the overall cut/fill balance reflected on the Earthwork Summary.

Please provide:

    • A clarification of how the excavation, embankment, and borrow quantities are intended to be balanced.
    • Any earthwork shrink/swell factors, subsidence calculations, surcharge quantities, over excavation quantities, unsuitable material removal quantities, or other adjustments used in developing the Q-1 summary that may speak to why there is more import borrow compared to the calculated roadway ex and embankment needs

 

Please provide clarification and/or revised quantity calculations if necessary so that all bidders may accurately determine the intended earthwork scope and associated Imported Borrow quantity.

Please confirm if the following interpretation is correct for the Special Provisions added to Section 90-1.02H.

Novato Bridge (Widen) and Novato Bridge (Replacement) mix design:

  • (C) May contain 25% - 50% cement (type II/V, V, or blended cement). No more than 50% allowed.
  • (F) May contain up to 15% fly ash.
  • (UF) Must contain 5% - 15% silica fume (or metakaolin or UFFA).
  • (SL) May contain 40% - 70% GGBFS.

This means slag must be used, as 100% of cementitious material cannot be achieved with the maximum limits placed on cement, fly ash, and silica fume, effectively eliminating fly ash as a viable option to maximize cement content while including the minimum slag content of 40% replacement. These requirements are far more strenuous than the standard spec for structures in a corrosive environment.

Early strengths and 28-day stengths are severely inhibited by slag. Girders have f'ci as high as 6.7 ksi (exceptionally high) and f'c at 9.1 ksi (also very high). Extensive R&D is required to source slag materials and test mixes to ensure a mix design which meets the above requirements can be made.

If this interpretation of the Special Provisions is confirmed, we respectfully request the bid opening be extended at least 28 days to allow time for sourcing material and testing various mixes to see if a viable mix can be found which reaches 9.1 ksi in 28 days.

Bidder Inquiries.Question:
Section 71-3.08A(1) states that no CIPP work is allowed from May 15 to October 15. Section 10-1.03 states that work within drainage channels is allowed only from May 15 to October 15, and section 13-12.03A restricts construction, use and removal of temporary creek diversion systems to the same May 15 to October 15 period.

Section 71-3.08A(1) also prohibits CIPP installation when a runoff-producing event is predicted within 4 days after curing unless a water diversion or temporary creek diversion system is in place. Under the dates above, a diversion cannot be in place during the period when CIPP work is allowed.

  1. Is the CIPP date restriction in section 71-3.08A(1) correct as written, or was it intended to read that CIPP work is allowed only from May 15 to October 15?
  2. If the restriction is correct as written, how is CIPP to be installed at culverts with flow, and is work at culvert inlets and outlets during the CIPP period considered work within drainage channels under section 10-1.03?
  3. Which locations are expected to require a temporary creek diversion system?

If the restriction in section 71-3.08A(1) is an error, please issue an addendum correcting it.

American Traffic & Safety Inc. (ATSI) provides comprehensive traffic control and construction support services designed to help keep projects safe, efficient, and compliant. Our experienced team is equipped to support projects ranging from local roadway improvements to highway and interstate construction.

Our services include:

Interstate and highway lane closures

Two-way flagging operations, with or without pilot vehicles

Road closure setup, maintenance, and detour implementation

Truck-Mounted Attenuator (TMA) services

Construction Area Sign (CAS) installation

Temporary erosion control installation

Traffic Control Equipment Rentals

ATSI also offers traffic control equipment rentals to support both short-term and long-term project needs, including:

Portable Changeable Message Signs (PCMS)

Arrow boards

Portable light plants

Whether providing complete traffic control operations, construction support, or equipment rentals, American Traffic & Safety Inc. is committed to delivering dependable, professional service while maintaining safety as our highest priority.
